key_insight: Increasing entanglement in the feature-map stage of a hybrid quantum classifier can improve generalization signals for epitope-receptor binding prediction, with the high-entanglement ZZ map showing the best overfit reduction.
engineering_relevance: For NISQ-era quantum machine learning, entanglement topology is a practical design knob that may matter as much as circuit depth when screening sparse biological binding data.
method: Classified Strong vs Weak PRRS epitope-receptor binding with a hybrid embedding-QNN pipeline.
Compared four feature-map settings: non-entangling Z, high-entanglement all-to-all ZZ, and two nearest-neighbour entangling variants.
Benchmarked against a classical CNN using a 40:30:30 train/validation/test split on 80 9-mer epitopes.
evidence_signal: The high-entanglement ZZ feature map achieved the lowest training AUAC and the highest test-to-training AUAC ratio while maintaining competitive test accuracy.
watch_item: The dataset is small and docking-derived, so the observed benefit may not transfer to larger, noisy, or hardware-executed quantum systems without further validation.
paper_title: Exploring the Effects of Entanglement on Quantum Machine Learning of Pathogen Epitope-Receptor Binding
